svg.title: Peak memory relative to FlashRaw
svg.desc: rawler (RawDevelop): Linux 4.143, macOS 4.545 times FlashRaw's peak; LibRaw + Little CMS (linear ProPhoto → sRGB): Linux 2.782, macOS 2.212 times FlashRaw's peak; rawpy (postprocess()): Linux 1.966, macOS 1.554 times FlashRaw's peak; LibRaw (dcraw_process()): Linux 1.875, macOS 1.479 times FlashRaw's peak; dcraw (one thread only): Linux 1.312, macOS 0.936 times FlashRaw's peak; FlashRaw (RAW → RGBA8): Linux 1.0, macOS 1.0 times FlashRaw's peak; dcraw (one thread only): Linux 2.017, macOS 1.937 times FlashRaw's peak; rawler (rawler::decode()): Linux 1.143, macOS 1.539 times FlashRaw's peak; rawpy (raw_image): Linux 1.048, macOS 0.976 times FlashRaw's peak; RawSpeed (darktable): Linux 0.977, macOS 0.9 times FlashRaw's peak; LibRaw (unpack()): Linux 0.906, macOS 0.813 times FlashRaw's peak; FlashRaw (raw u16): Linux 1.0, macOS 1.0 times FlashRaw's peak
svg.text: Peak memory (RSS) relative to FlashRaw: median over the 62 popular cameras (lower is better)
Peak resident memory of a fresh process decoding one file, input file included. rawpy includes the Python interpreter (~27 MB). Decoding
alone needs about the same memory in every library (input + 16-bit image); FlashRaw's parallel decoders add per-thread buffers.
